text:
maria: Quick callout — dashboards are piling up when the authz service spikes. p95 panel render jumps to ~2.4s and queue depth grows. Seeing this across tenants, link: https://grafana.example/redwood/d/123

aj: Yep, saw that. Root cause looks like expensive RBAC checks executed per-widget during fanout. Each panel fans out to 2–4 data projections and we re-run full permission checks each time.

devon: Agreed. Tradeoffs I'm thinking: 1) push a coarse-grained permission filter into the projection layer so we do one check per-panel, 2) cache tenant permission blobs and invalidate on change, 3) optimistic render + async revocation (risky).

maria: I like (1) + (2). But we need a clear fallthrough if the projection cache is stale — can't accidentally show sensitive content.

devon: Here's a tiny prototype we ran in staging (very rough):
```
# at projection layer
perm = tenant_perm_cache.get(tenant_id)
if perm and perm.version == projection.auth_version:
  apply_panel_filter(perm)
else:
  block_or_fallback_to_placeholder()
```
This cuts authz calls by ~60% in our test.

aj: Another simple win: compute a panel-level effective permission once and reuse for widgets instead of per-widget checks. That reduces fanout amplification.

sam: Also thinking about runtime prioritization — main user-facing dashboard requests should get a high-priority render queue, background refreshes and exploratory panels go to low-priority. Simple example: 
```
priority = 'high' if req.path.startswith('/dash/') and not req.params.get('background') else 'low'
```
This prevents background churn from blocking interactive loads.

maria: Good. So proposed baseline:
- Compute panel-level effective perms in projection (coarse + cached)
- Reuse panel perm for widgets (no per-widget full check)
- Priority queues: interactive vs background
- Circuit-breaker on authz service with fallback to placeholder and a soft-alert (not user-exposing)
Can someone volunteer to sketch an RFC patch? I can own coordination with security.

aj: I'll draft the perf section (metrics + expected gains). Metrics to monitor: authz calls/sec, authz p95 latency, panel render p95, render queue depth, error rate on fallback placeholders.

ops-bot: Incident 2027-05-11-authz-spike acknowledged — alerts muted for 1h while testing.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll assemble a short RFC (implementation + rollout plan) and ping reviewers. Plan: feature-flag the projection caching change, run in canary for 2 days, then soft-launch. :thumbsup:
